method: Each of the 129 features in 02-feature-list.md was compared with the code. built = the core of the feature as specified exists and a test or a `desk prove` check exercises it; partial = a real part exists, the missing part is named; absent = no code was found. A status is a judgement made by reading and searching; tests/desk/feature-status.test.ts checks that every feature has a row and every cited file exists, not that the judgement is right.

features.missing: adapter capability declarations; three adapters (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode), none for Gemini CLI, Cline or Cursor; the Copilot CLI local store holds turns and no token counts (checked 2026-10-24), so it cannot be read

figures are recomputed from rows through the Sessions screen, not from a signed dossier; the cause shares link to the day's sessions, not to the calls of each cause; the overnight gate section has been tried on a constructed gate database only
no status line reading has come from a real Claude Code session, so the Claude plan percent is NOT VERIFIED against the real tool; no menu-bar widget (the specification leaves it out)
idle and shared spend are not allocated (DF-095); the reported share has only been exercised on a constructed process; the CSV guard is not tried in a spreadsheet application
tried on the constructed sample and a log of the same shape, not on a real Claude Code log; no stop was ever tried on a live agent; the session timeline chart does not mark the stop point

the screen shows the questions and the command that answers one but does not answer them (the server is read-only by design); no-majority panels and inconclusive verdicts do not generate questions, only low-confidence links do

the hourly job has not been run by a real scheduler; the canary runs the model endpoint, not the owner's own agent and tool version; the pack is fixed and generic until tasks are captured from the owner's work (DF-036)

plan percent used and reset time are read from Codex logs and from a Claude Code status line command; each plan and window length is fitted separately (desk limits); desk runway and the Brief screen say whether a window will last, from how past windows of that plan ended (checked time-ordered on 110 Codex windows); no Claude reading has been captured yet (the user has to turn the status line on), and only the plus 5-hour window has enough history to forecast

types come from branch prefixes, ticket keys and labels, none of which this machine's real history has, so a type-specific estimate has only met constructed tasks; the scorecard is one person's rolling backtest
no desktop notification was shown on a real desktop and no webhook posted to a real service (stand-ins only); caps and pauses are tested through the rules, not a live gate

the approvals block is empty until the approval metrics (DF-049) exist; the calibration line waits for DF-034; a suggestion's effect is read from the logs or an upper bound, not tested by acting on it
